title: Quality of service
subtitle: OpenBSD 8.0 queues: hfsc classes attached to the interface

segments.text: The last piece is quality of service. This is the OpenBSD eight point zero queue syntax: a root class with ten megabits of bandwidth, a leaf class with two megabits as the default, and a rule that steers the traffic from the client to that leaf class.
pfctl shows the queues with their statistics, and the rule set shows the queue attached to the rule.
Now we move real traffic through the queue. On the server we prepare two megabytes and listen on port ninety ninety five.
And the client downloads it, through the firewall, through the class.
Two million bytes transferred, and look at the queue counters: the hfsc class counted the packets and the bytes. The scheduler is in the data path, not just in the configuration.
